questions.question: Pattadakal, a UNESCO world heritage site, is located on the banks of River ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malaprabha.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pattadakal,** a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is situated on the banks of the** Malaprabha River.**
 
• **It** provides evidence of the** wealth of Chalukyan architecture** from the **7th and 8th centuries.**
 
• It is renowned for its** intricately chiselled temples.**
 
• It comprises a collection of **10 significant temples,** each with a unique architectural style.
 
• The settlement was referred to as** "Perti gal"** by the **renowned geographer Ptolemy **(about 150 AD).
 
• It was even used as the **ceremonial centre** where** kings were crowned and commemorated**.
 
• The temple complex at Pattadakal features **Dravidian, Aryan, and a combination of the two architectural styles.**
 
• It is also the venue for the** Pattadakal Dance Festival **or **Chalukya Utsava **with performers from all over the world congregating here. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tungabhadra:**

 
 
• The majority of the Tungabhadra River's course is in the Indian state of **Karnataka**.
 
• It then passes through the border states of** Telangana and Andhra Pradesh** until coming together with the **Krishna River **next to Gundimalla village in the Jogulamba Gadwal district of Telangana.
 
• The river's water is renowned for being sweet and is regarded as the **sweetest water in the entire world.**
 
 
 
• **Ghataprabha:**
 
 
• The Ghataprabha River, a significant** right-bank tributary of the Krishna River**, travels** 283 kilometres** east of Chikksangam before joining the Krishna River.
 
 
 
• **Bhima:**
 
 
• The Bhima River often referred to as the** Chandrabhaga River,** is a significant river in both** South and Western India.**
 
• It travels through the states of** Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Telangana **for **861 kilometers** before emptying into the Krishna River.

questions.question: Phad paintings of Rajasthan belong to the following school of paintings
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mewar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Phad paintings of Rajasthan belong to the **Mewar ****school of paintings.**
 
• **Phad Painting:**
 
 
• It is a style of religious scroll painting and folk painting.
 
• **This style of painting is traditionally done on a long piece of cloth or canvas, known as phad.**
 
• The narratives of the folk deities of Rajasthan, mostly Pabuji and Devnarayan are depicted on the phads.
 
• It also depicts songs, dancing, and the narration of folklore and religious texts.
 
• The chitera, or the professional Phad painters developed the art form in the district of Pur, near Bhilwara, Rajasthan.
 
• The traditional painters migrated to Shahpura in the 16th century and then to the city of Bhilwara in the 19th century.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd33be3cbf297ee092a34af293bd07dfde71c38e5a8f6e70ed53638b9fcc6050.png] 

 
• **Mewar school of painting**

 
 
• It was developed in the Hindu principality of Mewār (in Rājasthān state).
 
• **The emergence of the Mewar School is widely associated with an early dated set of Ragamala paintings painted at Chawand in 1605 by an artist named Nisardin.**
 
• Painting in the eighteenth century increasingly slithered away from textual representations to courtly activities and pastimes of the royals.
 
• Mewar artists, generally, prefer a bright colour palette with prominent reds and yellows.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d673d59af10c6e5ca719a5512438e813525d2224c0c2772d12f32d31f5919bb3.png]

questions.question: Where is Great Stupa, one of the oldest structures, situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanchi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The stupa was **built by Ashoka** and was damaged during the break-up of the Maurya Empire.
 
• In the 2nd century B.C., it was completely **renovated during the rule of the Shungas.**
 
• The Great stupa consists of a **large hemispherical dome **which is flat at the top and **crowned by a triple umbrella or Chattra on a pedestal** surrounded by a square railing.
 
• Stupa at Sanchi has upper as well as lower Pradakshinapath or **circumambulatory path** and **four beautifully decorated toranas **indicating various events from the life of the Buddha and the Jatakas.
 
• **Great Stupa at Sanchi__** is one of the finest examples of **Buddhist Architecture.**

**​**** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

 
• **Dhamek Stupa **built by Ashoka is situated at Sarnath.

questions.question: Which of the following rulers constructed Shahjahanabad city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shah Jahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• Shah Jahan, the fifth Mughal emperor, is known for constructing the city of Shahjahanabad, which is now known as Old Delhi.
 
• He reigned from 1628 to 1658 and is also famous for commissioning the Taj Mahal, one of the **Seven Wonders of the World.**
 
• Shahjahanabad was established in 1648 and served as the capital of the Mughal Empire during his reign.
 
• The city is characterized by its grand architecture, including the Red Fort and the Jama Masjid, which are prominent landmarks.
 
• Shahjahanabad was built to be a symbol of Mughal grandeur and remains an important historical and cultural site in India.

questions.question: The Agra Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was primarily built by __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Akbar.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Akbar began the construction of the Agra Fort in 1565.
 
• The fort is an architectural masterpiece, representing Mughal grandeur.
 
• It served as the main residence of the Mughal emperors until 1638.
 
• The Agra Fort houses several notable buildings, including the Jahangir Mahal and the Khas Mahal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **Shah Jahan**__: Known for building the Taj Mahal.
 
• __**Aurangzeb**__: Last of the significant Mughal emperors.
 
• __**Jahangir**__: Son of Akbar, continued his architectural legacy.
